text:
The modern view of retirement needs to stop being seen as the primary goal and finish line for business owners and employees alike.

"Cash out and sail off into the sunset." Is a deeply flawed and concerning perspective that has all but destroyed the intergenerational glue that held nations together since the beginning of time.

It stems from the socialist/communist aspect of "utility" as it relates to members of the whole. When the usefulness (as defined by socialist and communist philosophy) of an individual has reached it's end, then the individual is sent away and discarded where any further utility they have stems from the resources they've maintained, which are drained through assorted means to and for the benefit of the state and other members.

What that currently looks like in reality is someone retires, buys the condo in Florida or Scottsdale, plays 5 rounds of golf a week, goes on a couple of cruises a year, sees their kids and grandkids a couple times a year, and slowly spends down their resources as they turn into pure consumers who spend most if not all of their remaining wealth on healthcare in the last 10 years of their life as their children and grandchildren struggle to establish themselves economically and plant their feet geographically. In only a few years, it's only around the birthdays of the deceased grandparents that their names are even brought up.

In contrast, a strong Christian family that stayed together looks nothing like that. The siblings and the in-laws do life together. Same town, same faith, same dinner table through the week. The grandparents are still a strong presence providing guidance and wisdom, and they offer free childcare. Fathers working alongside sons, and son-in-laws being adopted into the business.  The sibling's families and parents move as one unit with many parts, pulling the same direction. The business, tools, and land do not get sold to fund a ride off into the sunset. The grandchildren know their grandparents, and witness a faithful, fruitful, strong, and economically unified family that is strategically located geographically close to one another. The wealth and purpose stays together, so the next generation plants their feet where the family name already means something. 

This is the living legacy that teaches multiple generations the importance and process of stewarding well that which God has given and building something larger than any one family. 

If you haven't already, shed the hyper-individualism and plan now and begin working to build toward this vision in the decades to come. 

Generational faithfulness is a beautiful thing.

Trump unveils massive new pet project to transform Florida golf club into a new Camp David: 'It's a great idea'

President Donald Trump is moving to transform his private Trump International Golf Club in West Palm Beach into a secure, Camp David-style retreat designed to host future commanders-in-chief, international summits and foreign dignitaries.

Speaking to reporters in the Oval Office, Trump explained that the concept originated directly with federal security personnel rather than personal ambition, noting he agreed to the plan after being approached by law enforcement officials.

'This wouldn't be for me. This would be for all future presidents,' Trump said. 'This was suggested to me by the military and Secret Service... and if they want to do that, I'd be certainly willing.'

Having operated successfully for over two years, the Florida property offers distinct tactical advantages compared to standard golf developments.

Trump stressed that the facility lacks surrounding residential structures or high-rise vantage points, allowing security teams to achieve 'maximum safety' without needing to inspect adjacent private homes.

'You don't have houses with people hiding behind windows,' Trump pointed out, emphasizing that 'there are no high buildings looming over it.'

Yet in 2024, Secret Service agents thwarted an assassination attempt on Trump after a suspect armed with a scoped rifle lay in wait for hours at his West Palm Beach golf course.

In addition to physical security, Trump claims the location offers unmatched logistical convenience for official travel. 

'It's only about two minutes away from the airport, so they literally would be at that site, and they could spend the weekend there, like a retreat,' Trump stated, adding that security officials view the site 'as about as safe as they could possibly get.'

Harvey Oyer, a lawyer representing the Trump Golf Club, says there is no name picked out for it, although a SWR News reporter joked with Trump, asking if he would name it 'Camp Trump.'

Trump did not respond directly to the name change.

text:
🥊Welterweight Bout: Luis Francischinelli vs Will Rentz

🇧🇷Luis Francischinelli (6-1)
📍Fighting out of California Mixed Martial Arts | Representing Brazil
📏6'6" | Age: 30
🗓Last Fight: LFA 232 (May 15, 2026)
🧨6 KO/TKO, 0 SUB, 0 DEC
⭐Prospect Rating: ★★★☆☆

Francischinelli grew up in Itu, São Paulo, where his mother raised him alongside eight siblings in a household where gym fees were not exactly easy to find. A social project run with the Brazilian kickboxing confederation introduced him to the sport in 2010.

Years later, his mother scraped together enough money for him to travel alone to a South American championship. He left her in tears and returned as a champion. He claims close to 100 kickboxing bouts on the Brazilian circuit before the pandemic brought the competitive calendar to a halt.

At 25, Francischinelli and his then-girlfriend, now his wife, sold their car and motorcycle, contacted strangers for advice, and flew to California. He initially slept in a room behind Black House and shared space with whoever else was there. After hard sparring sessions with Alexander Volkov caught the attention of managers, he eventually moved to California Mixed Martial Arts.

The American chapter remains a calculated gamble. Francischinelli has described himself as a skinny fighter who once competed well below 170 pounds, and the move to California represented a chance to turn a Brazilian kickboxing career that was not paying the bills into something more sustainable.

🇺🇸Will Rentz (8-2)
📍Fighting out of Gracie PAC MMA | Representing United States
📏6'0" | Age: 27
🗓Last Fight: Combat Night Tampa (June 20, 2026)
🧨8 KO/TKO, 0 SUB, 0 DEC
⭐Prospect Rating: ★★☆☆☆

Rentz left Honolulu for the Tampa MMA scene and never really left the gym once he arrived. He fights and coaches out of Gracie PAC, owned by UFC featherweight Billy Quarantillo, who has been in his corner since the beginning of Rentz's professional career.

Quarantillo has also brought him into UFC camps as a sparring partner and had him in his corner for his own fights. Rentz has treated that experience as an education that could not simply be bought. Coaching has become another part of that development. He has said that explaining techniques to other fighters forced him to understand his own wrestling sequences more clearly.

The setbacks have been public. Following a 2023 loss, he framed his response in simple terms: average people are broken by failure. The nickname "Iron Will" comes from that mentality more than any marketing campaign.

His professional career has been almost entirely built around the Florida regional circuit, particularly Cage Fury and local Tampa shows.

👊There is not much about this matchup that inspires confidence.

Francischinelli is one of the more unusual welterweights on the regional scene. At 6'6" with an 83-inch reach, the physical tools are obvious, and he is a fun striker to watch. The problem is that his defensive flaws are just as obvious. He was recently exposed by Jo Piersma at LFA and has only one win since before earning this Contender Series opportunity.

He leaves his chin available, does not offer much on the ground, and relies heavily on his striking advantages.

Rentz is the opposite kind of prospect. His record is polished, but the quality behind it is not particularly impressive. He lost the one time he stepped up against a genuinely credible opponent, getting knocked out by Chris Alvidrez in 2023, and has spent much of the time since beating regional opposition.

He looks better on tape than the résumé suggests, but that is not exactly a high bar.

The physical gap should matter here. Francischinelli's length and striking volume should allow him to find Rentz early, and I expect him to land something before Rentz can turn the fight into the kind of wrestling-heavy contest that could expose Francischinelli's weaknesses.

This feels like a fight where the Contender Series format actually helps Francischinelli. He does not need to show a complete game. He needs to create enough chaos to land the big shot.

✅Luis Francischinelli to win by round 1 knockout

text:
New Injection May Ease Chronic Back Pain | Knowridge

Chronic back pain affects millions of people and can make everyday life difficult. Walking, working, sleeping, driving, or even bending down can become painful, and long-lasting pain can also affect mood and mental health.

One common cause is degenerative disk disease. The spine contains soft disks between its bones that act like cushions, helping absorb pressure and allowing the back to move.

As people get older, these disks can lose water, become thinner, and develop damage. This can lead to pain, stiffness, inflammation, and reduced movement.

Most treatments focus on controlling symptoms. Physical therapy, anti-inflammatory medicines, injections, and painkillers may help, while some people with severe problems eventually need surgery.

Researchers led by Dr. Douglas Beall at Clinical Radiology of Oklahoma have studied a different approach called viable disk allograft supplementation. Instead of only reducing pain, the treatment is designed to improve the condition of damaged spinal disks.

The procedure involves injecting donated disk tissue containing living cells into a damaged disk. Researchers believe this material may help create a healthier environment inside the disk and support tissue repair.

The treatment is minimally invasive and does not require major surgery. Patients receive the injection directly into the affected disk and can generally leave the medical facility the same day.

Early results have been encouraging. In a study of 50 people with chronic lower back pain caused by disk degeneration, about 60% experienced at least a 50% reduction in pain after treatment.

About 70% also had meaningful improvements in physical function. For someone living with chronic back pain, better function could make ordinary activities such as walking, exercising, working, and spending time with family easier.

Another possible advantage is reducing reliance on strong pain medicines, including opioids. These drugs can provide relief but may cause side effects and carry risks when used for long periods.

The treatment is part of regenerative medicine, a growing area of research that aims to help damaged parts of the body repair or restore function. Scientists are studying similar approaches for problems affecting joints, muscles, and other tissues.

However, the treatment is still being studied, and the early findings do not prove that it will work for everyone. Larger and longer studies are needed to determine how long the benefits last, which patients are most likely to improve, and how the treatment compares with other options.

The research on viable disk allograft supplementation was presented at the Society of Interventional Radiology Annual Scientific Meeting. If future studies confirm the results, the approach could eventually offer some people with chronic disk-related back pain another option besides long-term medication or major surgery.

CONDITIONAL STRATEGY
1. Current action: pass at the recorded asks. Do not chase the favorite merely because the sportsbook moved toward Edmonton.

3. Recheck liquidity, spread and order preview at execution. A limit order can still incur taker fees if it crosses the spread. Resting orders can be filled after adverse news; a lower fill price alone does not prove value.
4. Size from a predefined maximum loss. A losing YES or NO contract can lose its full purchase price plus fees. Avoid stacking correlated winner, puck-line and total positions as if they were independent.

METHOD / LIMITS
American odds convert to raw probability as |a|/(|a|+100) for negative odds and 100/(a+100) for positive odds. Normalize each two-outcome pair to total 100%. This removes the quoted overround proportionally; it is a single-book reference, not a proprietary model or a certainty about true probabilities.
Estimated taker fee = $0.07 × N × P × (1-P), rounded up to the next cent per order. Table shows the continuous one-contract equivalent; small-order rounding can cost more. All three series returned fee_multiplier=1. Winner series returned quadratic_with_maker_fees; spread and total returned quadratic. Actual order preview and current fee schedule control.
Net edge (cents) = benchmark percentage minus entry cents minus estimated fee cents. It excludes future exit costs and slippage. Purchases held to settlement pay $1 if the contracted outcome occurs and $0 otherwise. No trades were placed.
